name: Linguistics (Min)

rules.name: Core Courses
rules.desc: Select one course each from two of the three areas below.

rules.name: Language and Linguistics

children.name: A course in the history of a language (with the DUS)

rules.desc: Select one of the following, or, in advance consultation with the Linguistics Director of Undergraduate Studies, a course in the history of a language.

rules.name: Electives
rules.desc: The remaining courses toward the total 28 units are determined in advance consultation with the Linguistics Director of Undergraduate Studies. Students are encouraged to take at least one 200-level Linguistics course. Students may also choose to do independent work with a faculty member of their choice.

grading:
• No more than two courses may be taken on a credit/no credit basis (CR/NC).

• All required courses must be taken for a C- or better letter grade.
policies:
• All courses must be taken for at least three units.

• The courses counting toward the minor must be units beyond those needed to satisfy the student’s primary course of study.
transferPolicy: External credits are not accepted toward the Linguistics Minor.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 28 units: LINGUIST 1, core courses from two of three areas, and LINGUIST 150 or 160 (or a course in the history of a language the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves), each taken for 3 or more units and a letter grade of C- or better. The rest are electives you choose with the Director of Undergraduate Studies in advance and move in by hand. No more than two courses may be CR/NC; a third counts for nothing. Checked by hand: at least 3 units for every course, and that the courses go beyond what your major needs. External credit is not accepted.
